title: Wild Chicago night life and after-hours spots
summary: Clubs closed at midnight but after-hours spots stayed open; sporting women and con men did not bother anyone and strangers returned dropped money.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Chicago was pretty wild then? Sort of -- lots of night life and --
How long did it go on? When did these clubs at night close?
Well, when I left Chicago it was still going.

Oh, well, for instance you'd close at 12:00 o'clock now, then you could go on down to the after-hour spots, and stay until -- hours. Then you got ready to go home, sometimes 9:00, 10:00 o'clock, later than that. As long as you wanted to. They didn't close. No, they didn't close. And nobody bothered anybody. Nobody would take a dime from anybody. And Chicago was full of sporting women and confidence men. Because I know Harry Miller and all them confidence men were right there. And those sporting girls. But they didn't bother anybody, not a soul.
And people -- for instance, if you'd lose something, you'd lose $100.00 or something, they'd see you drop it, they'd say, 'hey, fellow, you dropped this money.'
